name: Marketing agency hero: headline scrambles through random characters on load before decoding into the final words
notes: Each [data-scramble] node runs its own requestAnimationFrame loop: over 900ms it locks characters left-to-right (Math.floor(progress*len) determines how many characters from the start are 'solved') while every unsolved character is re-randomized from CHARS on every single frame, giving the classic terminal-decode look. The two headline lines are staggered 450ms apart (scramble(node, 150 + i*450)) so the second line starts decoding just as the first is finishing, not simultaneously. Script sets each node's textContent to a fully-scrambled string synchronously before scheduling the animation, so there's no flash-of-final-text before JS runs. Under prefers-reduced-motion the whole IIFE returns early and the original textContent (already the final copy, since data-scramble mirrors it) is left untouched — no scrambling happens at all rather than a slowed-down version. The pulsing cyan 'Decoding audience signal' status dot in the top bar is a second, independent nod to the same motif and can be swapped for a real live-status indicator (open/closed, live chat, etc.) per the pattern in section 0008.
